title: Crumb and Punishment
description: The Maplewood Elementary PTA calls in to promote Saturday's bake sale, but treasurer Mildred runs the lemon-bar table like a cartel. Ronnie calls it community spirit, Barry calls it a felony, a terrified brownie guy tries to whistle-blow live, and Linda just wants the recipe.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight is all about giving back. The Maplewood Elementary PTA is here to tell us about Saturday's bake sale. Treasurer Mildred, welcome to the show.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, thank you, sugar. We've got cookies, we've got cupcakes, and we've got my famous lemon bars. <p:0.3> And everybody is going to buy something.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Everybody is going to buy something. That last part had a real edge to it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's just enthusiasm, Barry. Now Mildred, how do vendors sign up for a table?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Well sugar, it's simple. You bring your goods, I assign you a spot, and you pay the muffin tax. Ten percent of the table, right off the top, into the lockbox.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The muffin tax.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A small fee for the fundraiser. That's just good organization, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, hi, Mildred, it's Linda from the carpool line! Your lemon bars are to die for. Could I ever get that recipe?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Linda, sweetheart. <p:0.3> Nobody gets the recipe. People have asked. Those people don't bake at Maplewood anymore.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, that sounds lovely! I'll just bring my snickerdoodles then.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Yeah, hi. <p:0.3> Longtime listener. I do the brownie table. I just want to say, on the record, that the muffin tax is not... it's not exactly voluntary?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Darnell. Sugar. <p:0.3> Is that you on the radio?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: No. No, this is a different brownie guy. There's a lot of us. Allegedly.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that man is scared. That's a scared brownie man.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: He's just passionate about the fundraiser. Go on, Darnell.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: So last spring a guy named Phil tried to sell his cookies for a quarter under list. Undercut the table. And then Phil got... a visit. I didn't say that. I'm not saying Phil got a visit.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Phil decided to bake somewhere else, that's all. We wished him well. <p:0.3> We sent flowers to the spot where his table used to be.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's a threat. She is describing a hit on a man named Phil.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's just neighbors looking out for neighbors, Barry. That's good fellowship.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Aw, flowers! Mildred, you really do think of everything. Is that the lemon bars I smell?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Now Darnell, sugar, your brownie table did real well last month. Real well. <p:0.3> So we're adjusting your rate. It's not ten percent anymore. We're calling it the lemon bar tribute now.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: The tribute is forty percent, Mildred. Forty. <p:0.3> I'm whispering because she's in the cafeteria and I can hear the lockbox.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's a protection racket, Ronnie. The muffin tax is a protection racket.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's a tiered membership structure, Barry. Lots of charities do tiers.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: And honestly, sugar, the tribute's a little dated too. <p:0.3> Going forward, you don't pay the family. You bake for the family.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: I have a family, Mildred! I have my own actual family!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: You have the family now, Darnell.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: It does take a village! That's so true, Mildred.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Linda, she is conscripting him! She is forcing that man into a brownie cartel!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, that sounds lovely!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: It is not lovely, Linda! Run! Bake your snickerdoodles at home!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Nobody bakes at home, sugar.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Call somebody! Call the F B I!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Allegedly!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Recipe!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Alright, alright, beautiful energy, everybody. That's our show. Big thanks to Mildred and the whole Maplewood PTA. Come on out Saturday and support your local schools.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Before you sign off, sugar. <p:0.3> Snazzie FM had us on the air a full hour tonight. That's airtime. So the station owes a little muffin tax.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Oh. We don't really have a budget for...

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: There's a van in your parking lot, sugar. It's already loading the snack machine. <p:0.3> Don't make it a visit.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, would you look at that. A community partnership.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's extortion, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's a bake sale, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: And Darnell, sugar... we're not done. <p:0.3> There's a PTA across the river thinks they don't owe the territory. The Riverdale Boosters. Their fall carnival is going to have an accident. <p:0.3> You're gonna help me make sure of it.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: ...I never said that.
